meta.title: Bot RTS — program your bots, conquer the map
meta.description: A real-time strategy game in your browser where you build bots, write the scripts that run them 24/7, and compete on a persistent shared map.

hero.title: Program your bots. Conquer the map.
hero.subtitle: Build bots from modules, write the scripts that run them day and night, and take on other players on one persistent world.

build.title: Build
build.text: Deploy a base, craft modules in the factory and assemble them into bots: drills, scanners, guns, repair arms.

program.title: Program
program.text: Write JavaScript that drives your bots through a small API. Scripts keep running while you are away.

compete.title: Compete
compete.text: Mine, trade, fight and rebuild on a shared map where every other base is a player like you.

modules.title: Modules
modules.text: Every ability comes from a module you craft and fit. No drill, no digging: a bot is what you build it to be.

scripts.title: Real scripts
scripts.text: A real programming language in a sandbox, with a terminal, a file system on every bot and a typed API.

manual.title: Manual control
manual.text: Prefer to play by hand? Every action a script can take is also a button, and the game tells you what the bot sees.

world.title: A persistent world
world.text: The map never resets. Fog of war, radio links and limited energy make scouting and logistics matter.

showcase.title: A first miner in ten lines
showcase.text: This is all it takes to put a bot to work. The result of every call is a value, so a script handles an empty deposit instead of crashing.

free.a: Yes. You play in the browser; there is nothing to install or buy.

language.q: Which language do I write scripts in?
language.a: JavaScript, or TypeScript. The editor knows the whole API, and the documentation lists every call.

offline.q: Do my bots keep working when I close the page?
offline.a: Yes. Scripts run on the server around the clock, and you get notified about what happened while you were away.

api.q: Can I use my own tools?
api.a: The game has a public API with API keys, so you can build your own client or let an AI assistant play through it.

phone.q: Does it work on a phone?
phone.a: This site does. The game itself is built for a desktop screen, with windows, a map and a terminal.

meta.title: Privacy policy — Bot RTS
meta.description: What Bot RTS collects about its players, why, for how long, who receives it, and the rights players have over it.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Bot RTS is a browser game. This page explains what we collect about you when you play, why we collect it, and what you can do about it.

items.account: Account data: your name and email address, a hash of your password (never the password itself), and the time you accepted this policy.
items.game: Game data: your bases, bots, modules, items, files and scripts, the parts of the map you have seen, your achievements and notifications, and your settings.
items.terminal: Terminal logs: the commands you type and what the game answers, and the output of your scripts, so you can read them later.
items.technical: Technical data: the sessions you are signed in on (the browser name and when each was last used) and the address your requests come from, which is used to limit abuse.

purposes.title: Why we collect it
purposes.text: To run your account and the game you play, to keep other players and the service safe (limiting repeated password attempts, banning abuse), to send the emails you ask for (confirming your address, resetting a password, confirming a change), and to show you what happened while you were away. We do not sell your data and do not use it for advertising.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.text: We use one cookie, which keeps you signed in (it is HTTP-only and is sent only to the game's API), and your browser's storage for the access token and your language. These are essential, so no consent banner can switch them off. We set no analytics, advertising or other non-essential cookies.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.text: Account and game data are kept while your account exists. Terminal logs and notifications are kept for a limited time (notifications for 30 days). An account whose email was never confirmed is deleted after 7 days, and an account that has not been used for a year is erased after we have emailed you a notice 30 days ahead; an account that runs scripts, or has a paid plan, is not erased for inactivity. When you delete your account, your name, email, credentials and sessions are erased; the game data that the world depends on, such as the place of your base, stays without any link to you.

sharing.title: Who receives it
sharing.text: Your data stays with us. It is shared only with the services that do the work for us, such as the provider that sends our emails and the one that hosts the game, and with authorities where the law requires it. Other players see only what the game shows them: for example the name of a base they have scanned.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.text: You can see and change your name, email and password in your account page, and delete your account there; deletion is confirmed by an emailed link. You can ask for a copy of your data, ask us to correct it, or object to how we use it by writing to {email}. If you are in the European Union you can also complain to your data protection authority.

changes.title: Changes
changes.text: When this policy changes, its version changes too, and the new version is shown at sign-up.

home.title: Bot RTS documentation
home.lead: Everything you need to build bots, write the scripts that run them and play on the shared map. Start with your first base, then read the concepts. The reference pages are generated from the game itself, so their numbers are always the game's own.

firstBase.title: Your first base
firstBase.intro: Your base is the heart of your fleet: it holds your storage, the factory that makes modules and bots, and the radio that links your bots to you. You have one base at a time.
firstBase.step1: Sign up and confirm your email with the link we send you.
firstBase.step2: Press “Deploy your base to start” and choose the access password of the base. Other players need it to connect to your bots.
firstBase.step3: The game puts the base on a free cell of the map and gives it a starting kit of modules and resources. The map shows it in the middle of what you know.
firstBase.step4: A terminal opens on the base and a short checklist guides you through the first steps. You can skip it and bring it back from the settings.
firstBase.outro: If your base is destroyed it becomes a corpse base, and you may deploy a new one.

firstBot.title: Your first bot
firstBot.intro: A bot is a set of modules: it can do only what its modules let it do. You craft modules at the base's factory from resources and assemble them into a bot.
firstBot.part1: an engine and wheels (a chassis) to move
firstBot.part2: a battery for energy, and a generator with oil to refill it
firstBot.part3: a processor to run scripts, and memory (a drive) to keep them
firstBot.part4: a tool for the job: a drill to mine, a scanner to see, a gun to shoot
firstBot.how1: Open the Factory and craft the modules you need. Crafting takes time.
firstBot.how2: When they are ready, open the Assemble tab, tick the modules, name the bot and assemble it.
firstBot.how3: In the terminal the same is done with the commands craft and assemble.
firstBot.outro: The new bot appears next to the base. Click it on the map to open its control panel.

firstScript.title: Your first script
firstScript.intro: Scripts are JavaScript files on a bot's drive. They keep running while you are away.
firstScript.step1: Open the terminal of a bot that has a processor and a drive.
firstScript.step2: Type edit hello.js and write a script, for example the first one of the gallery.
firstScript.step3: Run it with run hello.js. The terminal answers “started” and an id.
firstScript.step4: What the script logs appears in the terminal; top lists the running scripts and kill stops one.
firstScript.outro: A script exports a function main(bot). Every call of the bot API returns a result that you check with ok.

map.title: The map and the fog of war
map.intro: The world is a grid of cells that never resets. A cell may hold a resource deposit, an item, a bot or a base.
map.fog: You see only what your scanners have scanned. A scanned cell is a snapshot: it shows what was there when you looked and fades with age. A cell you never scanned is black.
map.live: A scanner in live mode keeps an area up to date. Inside it you see changes as they happen, including other players' bots that come close. Switch it off and the area becomes an ageing snapshot.

ticks.title: Ticks
ticks.intro: The game advances in ticks, ten a second by default. Everything that happens in the world happens in a tick.
ticks.order: The orders of all players for a tick are collected first and then applied in a fixed order, so nobody gains from being faster than the others.
ticks.result: A call such as move or scan is queued; its result reaches your script at the start of a later tick. A script that waits for the result simply goes on when it arrives.

energy.title: Energy and time
energy.intro: Every bot has a battery, and everything it does costs energy.
energy.time: The world has one clock for everybody: an in-game hour is a real minute, so a day lasts 24 real minutes. The clock is in the corner of the screen, and the map goes darker at night.
energy.idle: Idle cost: each module drains a little every tick, even when it does nothing.
energy.operation: Operation cost: each action drains the cost of the module that does it.
energy.battery: The battery holds up to its capacity and never goes below zero.
energy.generator: A generator burns oil from the bot's storage and adds energy to the battery. It is strong, but you must bring it oil.
energy.solar: A solar panel burns nothing and makes energy from the sun: the most at midday, a tenth of it at night.
energy.sun: A solar panel makes the most at midday, about a half of that in the morning and in the evening, and a tenth at night. A base that does only light work lives on its panel; mining, driving and shooting all the time drain the battery faster than the panel fills it, and an oil generator is several times stronger.
energy.unpowered: A bot whose battery reaches zero is switched off: it does nothing and its radio link is down. It does not come back at the first unit of energy, but when it has grown back to 10, so that it does not blink on and off.
energy.empty: A bot with an empty battery can do nothing: its scripts wait until energy returns. Keep a power source in your bots, and oil if they run a generator.

opsBudget.title: The ops budget
opsBudget.intro: A script talks to the world through calls such as move, scan and dig.
opsBudget.cost: Each call costs operations. A bot has an operations budget per tick, given by its processor; when it is spent, its scripts wait for the next tick, and unspent operations are not saved.
opsBudget.free: Plain JavaScript between calls costs no operations, and sleep costs none either.
opsBudget.slice: But each script gets a short slice of real time per tick: an endless loop with no call in it is stopped. Put a call or a sleep in every loop.

weight.title: Weight and speed
weight.intro: Every module has a weight, and the weight of a bot is the sum of its modules.
weight.speed: A bot can move only if it has an engine and a chassis and its weight does not exceed what the chassis can carry. The heavier the bot compared with its engine, the more ticks one cell takes.
weight.assembly: The game refuses to assemble a bot that is too heavy for its chassis.

api.title: Script API reference
api.intro: A script is a file that exports main(bot). The functions below are methods of bot and also globals. A bot has a function only if it has one of the modules listed for it.
api.result: Every call except sleep returns a result: '{ ok: true, data }' or '{ ok: false, code, msg }'. Expected failures are values, not exceptions, so check ok before you use data.

modules.title: Module catalogue
modules.intro: The modules that exist, with the numbers of a new one. Modules of a higher class are researched from the class below.

recipes.title: Recipes
recipes.intro: What it costs to craft each module: resources and time.
recipes.research: Researching a higher class costs {costFactor} times the resources of the target recipe and {timeFactor} times its craft time.

botos.title: BotOS commands
botos.intro: Each bot runs BotOS, a small command line. These commands work in the terminal.

examples.title: Example scripts
examples.intro: Short scripts to start from. The test suite runs every one of them in the game's sandbox, so they work.

publicApi.title: Public API and API keys
publicApi.intro: The game has a public, versioned API (REST and WebSocket) that the official client itself uses, so you can build your own client or let a program play.

q1.q: Do my bots work when I am away?
q1.a: Yes. Scripts run on the server all the time, and notifications tell you what happened.

q2.q: Why does my script do nothing?
q2.a: Check that the bot has a processor, a drive with the file and energy in the battery, and that you check the ok of every result.

q3.a: It needs an engine and wheels, energy, and a weight the chassis can carry.

q4.a: The answer of a game call: '{ ok: true, data }' on success or '{ ok: false, code, msg }' when the game refuses, for example because a deposit is empty.

q5.q: Can other players see my bots?
q5.a: Only through their scanners, as snapshots, or inside their live areas. Connecting to your bot needs its password.

q6.a: The script API is in the reference, and the public API in its own page.

functions.sleep: Waits for the given number of milliseconds. It costs no operations.
functions.scan: A snapshot of the cells around the bot: x, y, type, content and resource of each.
functions.view: The changes of a live area since a game time, for a scanner in live mode.
functions.move: Moves the bot forward by the given number of cells.
functions.turn: Turns the bot a quarter turn to the left or to the right.
functions.dig: Mines the cell the bot faces; answers with the resource and the amount.
functions.mine: Mines the cell at the given coordinates, if it is within reach.
functions.pick: Picks up the item on the cell ahead.
functions.take: Takes an item (or the first one) into the bot's hands.
functions.drop: Drops what the bot carries on a cell.
functions.aim: Aims the weapon at a cell; answers with the distance.
functions.shoot: Fires at a cell; answers with the rounds fired and the hits.
functions.reload: Loads ammunition from the bot's storage into the weapon.
functions.enable: Switches a scanner, generator or battery on.
functions.disable: Switches a scanner, generator or battery off.
functions.getLocation: Where the bot is: x, y and z.
functions.getLinkStatus: The radio link of the bot to its base: connected or not, signal bars and hops.
functions.craft: Orders modules from the factory of the base.
functions.assemble: Assembles a bot from module parts at the factory.
functions.research: Starts the research of the blueprint of a higher class.
functions.learn: Learns the blueprint of an item the factory holds.
functions.repair: Repairs a module of a bot on an adjacent cell.
functions.disassemble: Takes a module of a bot on an adjacent cell apart for its parts.
